item.title: Daily report · 9 November 2026: Third Jordan-Syria Coordination Council Signs Eleven Agreements in Damascus
item.description:
Daily report · 9 November 2026
Third Jordan-Syria Coordination Council Signs Eleven Agreements in Damascus
People's mood: Leaning negative · The media: Mostly neutral
Coverage this cycle is dominated by the third Syrian-Jordanian Higher Coordination Council in Damascus, which produced eleven to thirty-five agreements and Jordanian condolences over the Daraa strike, alongside Syria's denial of sending troops to Yemen despite reports of a Saudi defense pact. Public commenters, especially on YouTube, voiced anger that no formal apology or compensation came for the Daraa victims, while others welcomed warmer Jordan ties. Heating-fuel shortages, new taxes, and the People's Assembly's repeal of immunity for administrative decisions drew mixed but mostly frustrated reactions, and Israeli gunfire on journalists and a shepherd in Quneitra added to a sense of continued vulnerability. Kurdish-language audiences focused separately on Rojava university integration, Kobani kidnapping and language-rights issues.
